angle: Treat AI like heavy equipment: commission it, certify operators, and instrument everything.
sourceTitle: Caterpillar is bringing to AI deployment what it learned from automating mining
linkedinPost:
AI deployments fail when we treat them like apps instead of assets.

TechCrunch reports how Caterpillar is porting lessons from autonomous mining to enterprise AI rollouts. It resonates: in harsh, safety-critical environments, success comes from commissioning, operator training, and telemetry—not just clever software.

My take from the field: treat AI like heavy equipment. Commission it with a checklist (data quality, failure modes, rollback), certify operators (who can start/stop, when to handover), and instrument everything (events, drift, human overrides). Then run a controlled ramp: one site, one shift, one clear KPI.

This discipline looks slow, but it’s the fastest path to scale because it avoids the rework that kills timelines and trust. Bonus: regulators and risk teams will work with you when you can show safety cases and post‑incident reviews.

If your AI touches customers, money, or safety, it’s not a toy—it’s a fleet.

What’s on your “AI commissioning” checklist before you go live beyond a pilot? #AITransformation #AIStrategy #EnterpriseAI #ForwardDeployedEngineer
